title: Softcut sentry & tenant quarantine journal
content:
Purpose: quick personal notebook for a lightweight ‘soft-cut’ sentry + tenant quarantine workflow. Intended as field notes while pairing with SRE and Solutions on Tuesday run. Keep terse; convert to formal playbook if pattern proves stable.

Context / Why this exists:
- We want an intermediate escape hatch between full rollback and broad pin (avoid broad customer impact).
- Use when a subset of tenants triggers persistent quality regressions or latency spikes after a model flip.
- Goal: isolate problematic tenants quickly, maintain service for others, collect richer signals for root cause.

High-level flow (staged):
1) detection -> sentinel alert -> manual quick triage (5–10m)
2) softcut: divert affected tenant(s) to pre-warmed fallback variant for 30–60m
3) observe telemetry (p95, error-rate, hallucination-rate proxy) for 30m windows
4) either reinstate, escalate to pin/rollback, or keep quarantined + deeper debugging

Quick checklist (for on-call / release lead):
- [ ] Confirm alert source(s) (Prometheus, tracing, RL metric). Signal names: inference_latency_p95, inference_error_rate, eval-regression-rate.
- [ ] Run quick cohort lookup: SELECT tenant, count(*) FROM requests WHERE model_version = X AND timestamp > now()-1h GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20
- [ ] Identify hot tenants (top 3 by requests or top 5 by error delta)
- [ ] Notify SRE + Solutions (Slack: #releases + @oncall)
- [ ] Execute softcut command (CLI below)
- [ ] Start 30m observation timer, capture sample logs & a handful of failing prompts
- [ ] After 30m evaluate: if metrics improved -> lift; if stable regressions -> escalate to full pin/rollback

Softcut mechanics (internal CLI / API cheat):
- quick pin command to route single tenant to fallback variant (example):
  redwoodctl route set --tenant tenant-id-123 --model fallback-v1 --duration 30m --reason "softcut auto-esc"
- to list active tenant routes: redwoodctl route list --filter tenant=tenant-id-123
- rollback to main for tenant: redwoodctl route delete --tenant tenant-id-123

Suggested softcut parameters (tunable):
- default duration: 30m (short, gives time to collect fresh telemetry)
- escalation duration: extend to 2h if evidence of slow-resolving degradation
- cohort size: start with single-tenant quarantine; if same failure cluster covers >5 tenants, consider broader cohort bucket (geo, client-version)
- traffic fraction: if tenant is shared across many client types, we can do fractioned cut: 50% -> fallback, 50% -> prod to compare in parallel (but increases noise)

Signal thresholds (working numbers — adjust per product):
- latency: p95 increase > +120ms and absolute p95 > 500ms for 5m window -> severity-2
- errors: error-rate increase >= +0.5 percentage points and absolute > 1.5% -> severity-1
- quality: automated eval regression (synthetic prompt set) delta >= 6% -> severity-1
- anomalous model output patterns: sudden frequency of ‘non-responsive’ token sequences -> investigate model tokenizer mismatch/quantization artifact

Data to capture during quarantine (make a zip):
- 50 example input prompts (raw and sanitized) from affected tenant across the 30m window
- full traces for 20 failed requests (ids)
- p95/p50/p99 time series for the tenant and aggregate baseline for last 24h
- model version, quantization flag, kernel/runtime variant (e.g., ttm-kernel-v2)
- any concurrent infra events (host restarts, kernel OOMs)

Notes-to-self / heuristics from pairing session:
- don’t escalate to org-wide rollback unless >10% global throughput impacted or multiple unrelated tenants fail simultaneously.
- softcut is conservative: prefer shorter durations, iterate. We can re-open a quarantine and extend if needed.
- explicit timebox for human review (30m triage + 30m observation) helps avoid impulse rollbacks.

Example play scenarios (micro-cases):
A) Single heavy tenant (adtech customer) sees p95 spike post-flip:
  - Softcut tenant -> fallback-v1 for 30m
  - Collect samples: see prompt pattern uses long context (2.5k) -> maybe kernel selection bug for long sequences on new runtime
  - Escalate to infra small-team: enable verbose kernel logs and confirm compilation path

B) Multiple small tenants with hallucination-like outputs:
  - Sampling + eval-run against curated prompt set -> if regression confirmed, pin model globally to previous version and open model-onboarding PR for deeper test cases

Operational caveats / gotchas:
- watch for cascading cold-starts when diverting many tenants to fallback; ensure fallback pool pre-warmed for expected QPS.
- Quarantined tenants may see different token accounting; coordinate CS billing note if outage >1h.
- Don’t forget to record the exact CLI args and who executed them (audit).

Postmortem anchors (if quarantine extended >2h or led to pin):
- timeline with exact route change timestamps
- compare request-by-request outputs across versions (diffs)
- root-cause hypotheses and short experiments tried (kernel patch, quant change, prompt rewrite)

Open questions / next steps (todo):
- [ ] Automate sentinel detection to suggest candidate tenants (pipeline query + top-5 heuristics)
- [ ] Add a ‘preview’ mode: mirror a small % to fallback w/o affecting production requests for A/B comparison
- [ ] Document cost/billing exposure for tenant quarantines longer than 1h and fallback pools used

Scratch ideas for UX:
- Redwood Console: small ‘Softcut’ button on tenant page to route + timebox with one click (pre-populated reasons)
- Show side-by-side tokenized model output diffs for a few sample prompts to speed triage

Final quick logs (today pairing notes):
- SRE: pre-warm script added to fallback pool; tested with synthetic ramp to 200qps -> cold-starts mitigated
- Solutions: want more client-visible reasons text in notification when we quarantine (friendly message)
- Follow-ups: I’ll draft a short runbook and pull request with redwoodctl wrapper for easier use.

— Alexis

(Notes: intentionally terse. If pattern repeats, convert to release-playbook entry + demo video for oncall training.)
